newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek yield curve flat, bonds ease, ecu/drs firm.
newsitem.headline: Greek yield curve flat, bonds ease, ecu/drs firm.

text.p: The Greek yield curve was little changed with short-term rates still holding high late Wednesday levels, bonds were retreating on the higher cost of carry and ecu/drachma was firmer, trading just above 310, dealers said.

"The yield curve is inverted with the short-end holding high late Wednesday levels," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Short-term depos are ranging in the 11.50-12.00 corridor and short-dated forwards are trading in the 11.20-11.90 band."
The trader said high short-term rates were offering good returns and some players from abroad were taking advantage of them.
"We are in a situation where one can reap the benefit of higher rates and likely gains from forex positions," the trader said.
The central bank surprised the market on Wednesday by draining 250 billion drachmas of 14-day funds at 11.90 percent in its regular Wednesday tender.
A pact of 200 billion drachmas was maturing so that a net amount of 50 billion drachmas left the system.
Prices of fixed coupon bonds were trading 10 to 15 basis points lower in early dealings, adversely affected by high short-term interbank rates, dealers said.

"Fixed coupon bonds opened slightly lower and their prices have slipped a bit more," said a dealer at a private bank. "We are currently 10 to 15 ticks lower and price levels are looking very attractive."
Traders said they expected selling pressure to ease with the approaching auction of three-, five-, seven- and 10-year fixed coupon bonds.
"We cannot go into the auction with short-term interest rates at these high levels," said a senior bond dealer at a private bank. "I expect much better market conditions by then."

Greece will reopen bids for three-, five- and seven-year coupon bonds on June 17 and auction its first-ever 10-year fixed coupon bonds. The amount is 50 billion drachmas for each maturity. The treasury auctioned three-year, 9.80 percent bonds, five-year, 9.20 percent and seven-year, 8.9 percent paper on June 19.
It will also auction 100 billion drachmas of 10-year fixed coupon bonds on June 19.
The mark was quoted at 158.79/84 from Thursday's 158.980 fix, the dollar at 274.70/80 drachmas from 275.320 and the ecu at 310.05/10 from 310.450 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma opened at 309.85/90 but has firmed to trade above 310 on some ecu buying for drachmas from abroad," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank.

The central bank's intervention in forex markets recently coupled with very attractive implied drachma rates from forex forwards convinced many players that the upside risk on ecu/drachma was limited, dealers said.
The National Bank of Greece quoted the following early rates:
** Overnight at 11.50-12.00
** One week at 11.50-12.00
** Two weeks at 11.50-12.00
** Three weeks at 11.50-12.00
** One month at 11.40-11.90
** Two months at 11.10-11.60
** Three months at 10.80-11.30
** Six months at 10.40-10.90
** Nine months at 10.20-10.70
** Twelve months at 10.10-10.60
--Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
